romania-2010.notes: Source 1: the crawled site mostly holds the Southeastern European regional contest pages for 2010 and 2011 and a 2016-2017 report; the Romania contest's own results page (source 2) is a separate capture. Confidence medium for that reason.

sources.evidence: The seed page is a frame set for the Romania Programming Contest with navigation for ACM 2009-2010, and the crawl holds 2010 regional pages and later Romania contest pages.
Four tables headed University, Team, Problems, Time: national final and the Bucharest/Iasi, Cluj and Timisoara subregions.
Table of 186 teams with columns Rank, Team, Institution, Solved, Time under the heading The 2010 Romania Programming Contest.

romania-2011.notes: Source 2 national final has 63 teams while source 3 lists 53; not reconciled.

sources.evidence: Four tables of the 2011 Romania Programming Contest: national final with columns A to J and three subregion tables.
Table of 53 teams with columns Rank, Team, Institution, Solved, Time under the heading The 2011 Romania Programming Contest.

romania-2012.notes: Source 1 mostly holds SEERC 2012 and 2013 pages and a 2013 Romania contest report; the 2012 Romania contest results are in source 2. Source 2 earlier verdict was correct, with roles now already corrected to scoreboard.

sources.evidence: The seed page is a frame set for the Romania Programming Contest and the crawl holds 2012 regional pages and 2013 Romania contest pages.
Tables for national final and Bucharest with columns A to L per team, plus Timisoara and Cluj subregion tables.
Table of 71 teams with columns Rank, Team, Institution, Solved, Time, Citation under the heading The 2012 Romania Programming Contest.

romania-2013.notes: Source 4 now serves an empty app shell (live copy of 2026-11-16). The report page of source 1 also holds the national final scoreboard (59 team rows, script-written), which is not a source of its own.

sources.evidence: Four-page site under acm.ro/Romania/2013 with a report dated June 2013 on the Romania Programming Contest, a results page and a problems page.
Results page with five tables: the Cluj and Timisoara tables hold 16 team rows each and three more tables are filled by script data holding 59, 76 and 11 rows.
Page titled 2013 ACM Romania Programming Contest problems with eleven links Problem A to K to contest 9268 on acm.tju.edu.cn.
The page is an empty application shell (hoj-vue, title with three Chinese characters, only a Loading indicator and a noscript notice) with no contest content.

romania-2014.notes: Source 1: the acm.ro crawl has no page of the May 2014 Romania Programming Contest; it holds SEERC 2014 and 2015 sites, the 2016 Romania report and 2011 pages (belongs to seerc-2014, seerc-2015, romania-2016, romania-2011). Source 3 is the ONIS 2014 olympiad ranking.

sources.disagreement: The earlier reader confirmed the site as a web source of this contest; the pages under /2014/ are the 2014 Southeastern European Regional Contest (Bucharest and Vinnytsia, 17-18 October 2014) and the /Romania/ report is the June 2016 Romania contest.
sources.evidence: The 150 files hold the 2016 Romania Programming Contest report, the SEERC 2014 and SEERC 2015 sites and the 2011 Romania contest pages; nothing in them is about the May 2014 Romania Programming Contest.
Table of 48 team rows with columns Rank, Team, Institution, Solved, Time, Citation headed The 2014 Romania Programming Contest.
Infoarena page titled ONIS 2014, Clasament Runda 4: ranking of individual participants in the national student informatics olympiad, not the ICPC Romania contest.

romania-2015.notes: Source 1 holds pages of seerc-2015, seerc-2016, romania-2011, romania-2012 and romania-2016, not to this contest. Source 2 is the 2012 Romania results (belongs to romania-2012, by capture date and content). Only source 3 is of this contest.

sources.disagreement: The earlier reader confirmed the site as a web source of this contest; the pages under /2015/ are the October 2015 Southeastern European Regional Contest and the /Romania/ pages are the 2011 site and the 2012 and 2016 Romania contests.
sources.evidence: The 150 files hold the SEERC 2015 and SEERC 2016 sites, the Romania Programming Contest reports of June 2012 and June 2016, pages of the 2011 Romania site and the 2012 results page; nothing in them is about the May 2015 Romania Programming Contest.
The results grid (problems A to L) is led by UNIBUC_BigDawgs with 11 solved and a penalty of 1226, which the June 2012 Romania report in the same crawl names as the winner of the 2012 contest.
Table of 46 team rows with columns Rank, Team, Institution, Solved, Time headed The 2015 Romania Programming Contest.

romania-2016.notes: Source 3 is the SEERC 2016 problem set (page title 2016 ACM SEERC), probably belongs to the SEERC 2016 contest; earlier reader confirmed it. Source 1 crawl is a series site with several editions; its seed page is a frameset shell. The national report gives a final on 16 June 2016 where the pack date is 2016-05-28; the report scoreboard has 67 teams against 59 in the standings.

sources.evidence: The crawl holds the 2016-2017 Romania Programming Contest report (national final of 16 June 2016) and the 2016 SEERC site alongside pages of other years.
Table of 59 team rows with Rank, Team, Institution, Solved, Time, Citation under the heading The 2016 Romania Programming Contest.

sources.disagreement: The earlier reader confirmed it as this contest's problem set; the page is headed 2016 ACM SEERC and the national contest report says its final ran on an online judge, so it belongs to the regional contest.
sources.evidence: The page is titled 2016 ACM SEERC: Set of problems, the problem set of the October 2016 Southeastern European Regional Contest, while the national contest report says its final used an online judge.

romania-2017.notes: Pack roles for source 1 are still web and problemset; the page is an infoarena judge contest page, so roles corrected to problemset as the earlier reader did. The scoreboard (71 rows) is larger than the 52-team standings and does not mark which rows are official.

sources.evidence: Infoarena page headed ACM ICPC Faza Nationala 2017 with round rules and a table of 9 problem titles, not a site of the organisers.
Table of 71 rows with Pozitie, Nume, nine problem columns, Scor and Penalizare, titled Clasament ACM ICPC Faza Nationala 2017.
Table of 52 team rows with Rank, Team, Institution, Solved, Time under the heading The 2017 Romania Programming Contest.

romania-2018.notes: Source 2 has 69 rows against 39 official teams in source 3; it mixes in other accounts. Pack date 2018-09-30 differs from the page's 29 September.

sources.evidence: Infoarena contest page titled 'ACM Romanian Collegiate Programming Contest 2018' with a table of 10 task rows and the rules, no site pages of its own.
Infoarena results table of 69 team rows with Pozitie, Nume, nine task columns plus 'Listare surse [Not a Task!]', Scor and Penalizare.
Table of 39 ranked teams with Rank, Team, Institution, Solved, Time and Citation under the heading 'The 2018 Romania Programming Contest'.

romania-2019.notes: Pack date 2019-09-29 differs from the page's 28 September. Source 2 has 82 rows against 54 teams in source 3.

sources.evidence: Infoarena round page 'Romanian Collegiate Programming Contest 2019' with a table of 11 task names, authors and rules, and no further site pages.
Infoarena results table of 82 rows with Pozitie, Nume, 11 task columns, Scor and Penalizare.
Table of 54 ranked teams with Rank, Team, Institution, Solved, Time and Citation under the heading 'The 2019 Romania Programming Contest'.

romania-2021.notes: Pack lists this source as web+standings; copy has no standings rows. The contest's start (2021-10-31 08:00 UTC, five hours) is only an epoch timestamp in the page data, so contest_date is left null.

sources.evidence: Virtual Judge contest page whose status table is empty and whose embedded contest data lists 13 problems A to M; no standings rows are present.

romania-2022.notes: Pack lists this source as web+standings; copy has no standings rows. Contest start is only an epoch timestamp in the page data (2022-11-20 08:00 UTC, five hours), so contest_date is null.

sources.evidence: Virtual Judge contest page 'RCPC 2022 Universities' with an empty status table and embedded contest data listing 15 problems A to O; no standings rows.

romania-2023.notes: The Gym contest (104782) appears to be the Day 2 set (attachments named Day 2); the post says Day 1 is on Kilonova and was to be added to Gym later. Standings rows are all Ghost participants.

sources.evidence: Codeforces Gym standings titled '2023 Romanian Collegiate Programming Contest (RCPC)' with 107 team rows and columns A to M with tries and times.
Gym dashboard of '2023 Romanian Collegiate Programming Contest (RCPC)' with a table of problems A to M and links to statements and an editorial.
Codeforces blog post 'RCPC 2023 on Gym' by the contest's coordinator, announcing that the contest was posted on Gym.

romania-2024.notes: Sources 1 and 3 have no copy. Source 2 has 95 rows including one admin account (RCPC Admin) and individual-looking names; official teams are not marked.

sources.evidence: Published Google Sheet 'RCPC 2024 full rank' with 95 team rows and columns A to M plus N = B with times and failed attempts.

romania-2025.notes: Source 3 is only a wrapper around the sheet that is source 2; its roles are empty because it holds no results itself.

sources.evidence: Site titled 'RCPC 2025 - Romanian Collegiate Programming Contest' with a front page, a schedule page and an about page naming 9 November 2025.
Published sheet 'RCPC 2025 ranking public' with 104 ranked team rows with Rank, team, Award, Solved and Penalty and no per-problem columns.
Stub page 'Results - RCPC 2025' with a heading, one sentence and an embedded frame of a published Google Sheet; the page holds no results itself.

romania-2026.notes: Source 2 is the published-sheet wrapper of the same sheet as source 3 and holds no table in our copy; source 3 is the sheet itself.

sources.evidence: The page is titled 'RCPC 2026 - Romanian Collegiate Programming Contest' and gives the contest dates and location.
The page holds only the title 'RCPC 2026 ranking public - Google Drive' and one sheet tab name, with no table rows.
A table of 96 team rows with rank, university and site, team name, award, solved and penalty, under a statistics line of 96 teams, 14 problems.
